description: Prove the three features in real headless Chrome over localhost (a secure context), then document everything and bump the version. Depends on FEAT-001 and FEAT-002; fix any bug the browser run finds in the files that own it (record it in findings).
steps: Create tools/e2e-intercom.mjs (Node built-ins only): spawn `node src/server.js` from the repo folder with env PORT=<spare port>, DEMO_MODE=true, ADMIN_TOKEN=<random test value>, NOISE_METER=on, and a ROOMS_JSON with room 'front'; spawn chrome-headless-shell (path in context.json) with --remote-debugging-port, --use-fake-device-for-media-stream, --use-fake-ui-for-media-stream, a temp --user-data-dir; talk DevTools protocol through a tiny client over Node's global WebSocket (Target.createTarget, Runtime.evaluate, Page.navigate, Emulation.setGeolocationOverride, Browser.grantPermissions for audioCapture and geolocation, Network events). Always kill both processes and remove the temp dir, also on failure; print only pass/fail lines, never the token.

Scenarios, each asserted: (a) before any press: tablet page at http://localhost:PORT/room/front?kiosk=1 has made zero RTCPeerConnection (hook window.RTCPeerConnection before load with Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument), the only microphone use is the noise meter with #noiseNotice visible, #micNotice hidden, and no network request body from the tablet contains audio (only JSON to /api/...); dashboard (opened with the token in sessionStorage) shows the tablet with a noise level and dB within ~15 s and the geolocation override as text with an Open map link; (b) press with no dashboard open -> 'Nobody is signed in' text, still no peer connection, no new getUserMedia; (c) dashboard open, press -> ring banner appears, tablet says Calling and still has no peer connection and #micNotice hidden; admin Answer -> #micNotice shows, connected on both sides, admin <audio> receives inbound audio (RTCPeerConnection.getStats inbound-rtp audio bytesReceived grows) and the tablet side sends audio, noise meter paused during the call; (d) hang up from the door -> all tablet tracks readyState ended, #micNotice hidden, meter resumes; repeat with hang-up from the dashboard; (e) unanswered ring times out (start the server with INTERCOM_RING_SECONDS=10) -> tablet says Nobody answered; (f) a second dashboard tab answering after the first gets 'Already answered'; (g) server log captured from the server's stdout contains the 'Intercom:' started/answered/ended lines with the 'administrator token' wording and contains no 'v=0' or 'candidate'; (h) a page opened with ?nostream=1 neither shows the call button nor opens a microphone.
Run it: `node tools/e2e-intercom.mjs`; it must exit 0. If a scenario fails, fix the owning file (public/*, src/*), re-run `npm run check` and the script until both are green.

Docs: INSTALL-UBUNTU.md new section '12f. Door intercom, noise level and location' (what it does, the exact Fully steps: set each tablet's Start URL to https://conference.orlandofoods.com/room/front?kiosk=1 and .../room/back?kiosk=1, keep Microphone Access, Geolocation Access on; Android Location switch on and Fully allowed Location and Microphone in Android app permissions; nothing else changes in Fully, and do not start Fully's own sound detection or audio upload features; the camera address list FULLY_CAMERA_HOSTS keeps the tablet IPs; how to roll back = put the old http address back), update section 11 (tablet URLs) and 13/12c nginx note (tablets can use https, no nginx change needed); README.md (features, settings, Security: sound only during a call the door starts, never stored or logged, badge, noise sends numbers only); `.env.example` (the 7 new settings with comments); `deploy/nginx-https.conf` header comment (tablets may use the https address now); CHANGELOG.md new '## 2.2.0' section; bump version to 2.2.0 in package.json, both places in package-lock.json, and anything test/project.test.js ties to it (grep `2\.1\.0` across tracked files, e.g. DEPLOY-CHECKLIST.md 'Running version', scripts/smoke-test.sh if it hardcodes). Write limits honestly (LAN-only calls, thresholds untuned, ring tone may be blocked).

`git add` new files, `bash scripts/update-manifests.sh`, `npm run check`, commit locally on main (e.g. 'Intercom, noise level and location: browser check, docs, version 2.2.0'), never push, never deploy.
acceptance_criteria: `node tools/e2e-intercom.mjs` exits 0 and its output lists every scenario a-h as passed
`npm run check` passes with the version bump
Docs, .env.example, CHANGELOG and manifests updated and committed; `git status` clean; nothing pushed
No secret appears in any committed file or script output
findings: Committed on main. node tools/e2e-intercom.mjs exits 0 with scenarios a-h all PASS in real headless Chrome (no bug found in public/* or src/*); npm run check: 264 tests pass. Script uses a random test token, spare ports, kills server and Chrome, removes temp dir. Scenario f simulates the click race by replacing dropRing in the second dashboard page so its banner stays (otherwise the 'taken' event hides it). Docs: INSTALL-UBUNTU 12f, README, CHANGELOG 2.2.0, .env.example, nginx comment; version 2.2.0 in package.json, lock, DEPLOY-CHECKLIST; manifests regenerated. Not verifiable here: real tablets/Fully, ICE across office network, real dB thresholds. .agents/ left uncommitted.
